findings.heading: Missings / Manques
findings.proposition: The French states that linear time-series imputation draws a straight line between the last non-missing values and the missing values; the English states it draws a straight line between the last non-missing value and the NEXT non-missing value.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader is given a definition of linear interpolation that has no second anchor point, so they cannot understand or reproduce what na_interpolation() does, and may believe imputation is anchored on missing values.

findings.heading: Load data / Chargement des données
findings.proposition: The French instructs the reader to import the counts data with the import() function of the rio package; the English has no such sentence and the adjacent chunk imports with appliedepidata::get_data(name = "campylobacter_germany").
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader looks for a file to pass to rio::import(), does not find one, and cannot reconcile the instruction with the code chunk immediately below that calls appliedepidata::get_data().

findings.heading: Fourier terms (outbreak detection) / Termes de Fourier
findings.proposition: The French says the second fourier() output predicts the year of interest "by defining the fourier() parameter"; the English says it is done by defining the `h` argument, which is what the adjacent chunk uses (h = num_weeks).
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader is not told which argument controls the forecast horizon, so cannot adapt the code to a different prediction period and will not connect the text to `h = num_weeks` in the chunk.

findings.heading: Relation of two time series > Descriptive analysis
findings.proposition: The English subsection heading "### Descriptive analysis" and its whole introductory paragraph have no counterpart in the French, where the basic_plot_bivar chunk follows the join chunk with no heading or prose.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader meets a bivariate plot with no introduction, no instruction to plot the data first, and no cross-reference to the pivoting-data chapter, and the section structure no longer matches the English table of contents.

findings.heading: Relation of two time series > Descriptive analysis
findings.proposition: The English states that the plot shows a clear relation in the seasonality of the two variables and that temperature might peak a few weeks before the case number; the French states neither.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader is not told what to look for in the plot, and loses the observation that motivates the four-week lagged temperature variable built two subsections later.

findings.heading: Interrupted timeseries / Série chronologique interrompue
findings.proposition: The French symbol glossary defines "Î'(x" as the indicator function while the French displayed equation writes that term as "Î´(t-t_0)"; the English uses one symbol, δ, in both places (β and δ are corrupted to Î² and Î´/Î' throughout the French).
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader cannot map the glossary entries onto the terms of the equation, so the definitions of the intervention terms β2 and β3 become unreadable and the model specification cannot be checked.

findings.heading: Time series data / Données de séries temporelles
findings.proposition: The English states that cases drop in the last week of the year before increasing in the first week of the next year; the French states only that there is a reporting problem at the start of each year and that counts increase in the first week of the following year, with no statement that counts fall.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader learns only half of the year-boundary artefact and may not understand why weeks W51-W02 are later set to missing and interpolated.

findings.heading: Autocorrelation / Autocorrélation
findings.proposition: The English explains that the ACF value at lag 0 is always 1 because it is the relation between an observation and itself; the French says only that it shows "the relation between the two", without naming what the two are.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader is given no reason why the lag-0 autocorrelation equals 1 and may mistake it for a property of the data rather than an identity.

findings.heading: Autocorrelation / Autocorrélation
findings.proposition: The English notes that the lag-0 line is not shown in the plot produced by ACF(); the French omits this note.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader looks for the x = 0 line described in the text, cannot find it in the output, and may think the code or the plot is wrong.

findings.heading: Prediction validation / Validation de la prédiction
findings.proposition: The English gives the reason for validating on the latest year before the present one as "because you don't yet know the counts for the current year"; the French replaces this with the circular "because you cannot predict the current year" and never states that current-year counts are unknown.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader is not told why the current year is excluded from validation, so cannot judge when the same approach applies to their own surveillance data.
